name: Milemarker
label: Jade Tree
lede: A Chapel Hill band that pitched itself as sci-fi soundtrack music spliced with Black Flag, wrote songs about sex jams and the CIA over synthesizers, and never quite got around to breaking up.

eras.title: Synthesizers in Chapel Hill
eras.text: Milemarker started in Chapel Hill, North Carolina in 1997 and put out records at a sprint, on a string of small labels. The early sound leaned on electronics; the guitars got heavier later.

years.h: Milemarker forms in Chapel Hill, North Carolina
years.p: Milemarker starts in Chapel Hill and plays both the Chapel Hill and, later, Chicago underground scenes. The band describes its sound as sci-fi soundtrack music genetically spliced with Black Flag.

years.h: Two albums in one year: Non Plus Ultra and Future Isms
years.p: Milemarker releases Non Plus Ultra on Paralogy and Future Isms on Stickfigure, plus the Receiver 7-inch on Clocked Out.
Milemarker shares a 7-inch with the Seattle band The Blood Brothers on Boards Don't Hit Back, and also releases the Sex Jams 7-inch on Bloodlink and Changing Caring Humans on Stickfigure.

eras.title: Frigid forms on Jade Tree
eras.text: Jade Tree gave Milemarker a bigger stage just as the label was known for emo. Milemarker answered with keyboards, male/female vocals, and song titles about server errors and the CIA, while the band moved its base from Chapel Hill to Chicago.

years.p: Released with Lovitt Records and Jade Tree. Songs include Sex Jam One: Sexual Machinary, Server Error, and Internet Relay Chat with the Central Intelligence Agency.
years.xp: The label copy sold it on keyboard and electronic sections, ethereal male/female vocals, and a precision you don't expect from guitar, bass and drums.
play: Internet Relay Chat with the Central Intelligence Agency

years.p: Milemarker's single for 208 Records comes out the same year as Frigid Forms Sell.
Seven long songs, from Shrink to Fit to The Installment Plan. Milemarker billed the result as epic, sprawling rock anthems built from electronics and hardcore punk.
Six songs: three heavy ones, then three electronic tracks the label compared to Kraftwerk's precision and Prince's funk. Pitchfork's Chris Ott reviewed it that October.
years.xp: Released with Day After and packaged with live footage, the EP also carries Lost the Thoughts but Kept the Skin, a song from Anaesthetic. Milemarker's lyrics lean on wordplay and irony about materialism, technology and gender roles.

eras.title: Ominosity, then the lights go off
eras.text: Milemarker's members split their time with a side band, made one more record with heavier drums and knottier guitars, and then quietly stopped. Nobody announced a breakup.

years.h: Side band Challenger releases its debut
years.p: Al Burian, Dave Laney and Tim Remis release Give People What They Want in Lethal Doses as Challenger.
Heavy percussion, intricate guitars and a dynamic vocal attack, on songs like Pornographic Architecture and Landlord. It is Milemarker's last album for eleven years.
From 2005 to 2008 Milemarker neither records nor tours, but never officially calls it quits.

eras.title: The original lineup, one more lap
eras.text: Three years after going quiet, Milemarker's original members came back together for a European tour and a first hometown show in two years.

years.h: Punknews: Milemarker will reunite for Europe
years.p: Punknews reports the band, once of Jade Tree and Eyeball Records, will tour Germany and Denmark later in 2008.

years.h: Chapel Hill's Milemarker plays its first show in two years
years.p: Independent Weekly marks Milemarker's return at home. The original members go on to play a 12-date European tour, including a festival in Lärz, Germany.

eras.title: Conditional love
eras.text: Members drifted into other projects, but Milemarker came back with its first album in more than a decade and a U.S. tour.

years.h: Dave Laney's new band Bee Control
years.p: Punknews premieres Bee Control, Dave Laney's project with [[Pelican|5a797e16-f69a-4957-820f-1152ec19d236]] guitarist Trevor de Brauw and Theo Katsaounis of [[Joan of Arc|0f2fea44-7e03-47f9-86e6-91d0a22fd0ee]].
Milemarker's first new release in a decade, a preview of the album to come.

years.h: Overseas, Milemarker's first album in eleven years
years.p: Nine songs on Lovitt, including one named for Carrboro, the town next door to Chapel Hill where the band began.
Milemarker plays a U.S. tour, twenty years after forming in Chapel Hill.

sources.title: Independent Weekly: Chapel Hill's Milemarker plays its first show in two years (June 28, 2008)
